title: dict: GC-native persistent ordered tree with lazy values; sets and priority queue on it
description: The largest gap for AoC: there is no map with non-string keys and sub-linear insert. Blocks take symbol keys with linear lookup (src/eval/stg/block.rs:462) and O(n) merge (2025 day 11's DP table takes ~4 s this way); sets copy on every add. Memoisation, cycle detection (state -> step), Dijkstra distances, frequency counts and 2020 d15 / 2024 d22-style puzzles all need it. Proposal: a HAMT (or similar) intrinsic keyed by primitives (ints, strings, symbols) with O(log n) assoc/dissoc/lookup, plus set operations on the same structure, and prelude wrappers (map.from-list, map.get-or, map.assoc, map.update-with, map.keys/values/entries, frequencies). New intrinsic: owner merges.
acceptance_criteria: Design note agreed with the owner covering node layout, GC tracing/evacuation, key hashing/equality (OrderedFloat semantics, list keys), sorted iteration, rendering and typing; dict API above implemented with docs, types and tests; sets on the same nodes with existing set tests passing and to-list order unchanged; 1e5 int-key inserts + lookups and 1e5 set adds each in well under a second with bounded RSS; GC-churn benchmarks 002, 005-009 not regressed (protocol-backed numbers); passes under EU_GC_VERIFY=2, EU_GC_POISON=1, EU_GC_STRESS=1.
notes:
2026-11-11 history check. Prior attempt: persistent blocks on im_rc::OrdMap (eu-m59i, PR #319 merged opt-in, phase 3 made every block literal an OrdMap; PRs #386/#387 closed; removed by PR #388) -> ADR-001 in docs/development/architectural-decisions.md: deferred because the GC never runs Drop, so Rc nodes leaked (220-580% regressions on GC-churn benches); a finaliser list (PR #387) was judged too costly; a Meta default tag mismatch broke 62 tests. eu-hmji (im::HashSet sets) closed unbuilt. ROADMAP DS1 (June 2026 reset) sets the direction: GC-native CHAMP nodes stored inline in the GC heap as traced objects, no Rc, no finaliser, deterministic order. Constraints for this bead: (1) no Rust-heap ownership in GC cells - do NOT use im/rpds/imbl; (2) nodes are GC heap objects whose child refs are marked, scanned and updated on evacuation, safe across allocation; (3) keep blast radius small: a new opt-in map/set type, not a change to block representation, so GC-churn benches 002, 005-009 are unaffected; (4) deterministic iteration (sorted or insertion order), never hash order, incl. render and blob; (5) keys primitive (Num via OrderedFloat incl. NaN/-0, Str, Sym) with strings held as GC heap strings, not Rust String; (6) every tag check/intrinsic/render/printf/typecheck IntrinsicType/parallel serialise handles the new type; (7) GC area: validate under EU_GC_VERIFY=2, EU_GC_POISON=1, EU_GC_STRESS=1; two independent rig-reviews; owner merges (new intrinsic). Reuse for DS1 blocks later. Relates to eu-iv2j.1 (DS2, general vec) and eu-oaz72.5 (P0 finalisation).
2026-11-11 owner design decisions:
1. Name: dict (map is the prelude function).
2. Keys: primitives (number, string, symbol; bool and null once eu-oaz72.30 lands) AND lists of primitives (e.g. [x, y] coordinates, 4-tuples), deep-forced and hashed structurally; once forced they hold no heap references.
3. Values: arbitrary and LAZY (stored unforced), so self-referential memo tables work, e.g. memo: dict.of(states map(...)) whose entries refer to the dict.
4. Iteration order: sorted by key (matching set.to-list); helpers for insertion order only if needed.
5. API: dict.of(pairs) with dict.from-list alias (per eu-oaz72.32 convention), to-list (pairs), get(k), get-or(k, d), assoc(k, v), dissoc(k), update(k, f, d), contains?, size, keys, values, merge-with(f), dict.from-block / dict.to-block.
6. Rendering: exports as a mapping in key order with keys stringified; clear error for list keys in formats that cannot represent them (e.g. JSON).
7. Types: a typed dict(k, v) in the checker from the start.
8. Sets reimplemented on the same CHAMP nodes in the same work (set = dict with unit values), making set.add/remove O(log n).
Constraints from the history (see earlier note): GC-native nodes, no Rust-owned storage, opt-in type (blocks unchanged), deterministic order, GC verification modes, two rig-reviews, owner merges.
2026-11-11 correction: dict is independent of blocks. Blocks (ROADMAP DS1, eu-iv2j.1) stay cons-lists for this work; when DS1 is scheduled it chooses its own structure (it may reuse dict's if that fits). Ignore the earlier 'reuse for DS1 blocks later' wording.
2026-11-11 owner decision: GC-native nodes, no im/rpds/imbl and no finalisers. Structure: persistent ORDERED TREE first (e.g. B-tree or balanced binary tree as traced GC heap objects): sorted iteration for free (decision 4), O(log n) get/assoc/dissoc, plus min, max, pop-min, pop-max and range(lo, hi) - which makes dict the priority queue (key [priority, seq]) and absorbs eu-oaz72.22. Total key order across types: numbers < strings < symbols < lists (lexicographic); bool/null placement to decide with eu-oaz72.30. Measured context (Rust, im-rc 15, one run, measured-single): OrdMap beat HashMap on insert (56 vs 116 ms at 1e5), lookup, sorted iteration (1 vs 10 ms) and [x,y] keys; HAMT min is a full scan. A CHAMP may follow later if a hash structure is needed (possibly for blocks, ROADMAP DS1) - separate decision.
2026-11-12 acceptance addition: a counting-by-key DP benchmark - AoC 2024 d11-style stone counting (public rules: 0 -> 1; even digit count -> split halves; else * 2024) from synthetic starting stones, 75 blinks, using dict update/merge-with per step - completes in a few seconds with bounded RSS (today: 25 blinks 1.3 s, 40 blinks 15 s / 8 GB, 75 blinks OOM). Dict values are arbitrary, so counts ~1e14-1e15 stay exact (unlike f64 storage, eu-oaz72.10).
2026-11-12 design note drafted: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-12-dict-design.md (PR #1134, held for owner agreement). Summary: weight-balanced binary tree (recommended over B-tree) of immutable DictNode heap objects {size, left, right, key: DictKey, value: BcValue}; keys Int/UInt/Float(OrderedFloat)/Str(heap string)/Sym/List(inline key list), exact ints, 1 = 1.0, comparison only (no hashing); thunk values wrapped in one-slot env-frame value cells so get memoises; render via block path in key order; dict(k, v) type; sets = dict with unit values; 5 PRs (nodes, core intrinsics, ordered ops + Dijkstra/benchmark, render+typing, sets). Nine open choices in note §11 await the owner.

2026-11-12 owner accepted every recommendation in the design note (PR #1134 comment 'Accept recommendations') and merged it (bc7901f). All 12 OPEN choices in note §11 are decided as recommended. Design-note part of acceptance met; implementation waits on eu-oaz72.5. The note's Status line on master still reads 'Draft for owner agreement' — update it with PR 1 of the implementation.
2026-11-14 PR 4 design (render + typing + docs; branch eu-oaz72.21/dict-render-typing). RENDER (note §8): new intrinsic DICT.RENDER_VIEW(x): for a dict returns its entries as a list of BlockPair(symbol, value) in key order (values as stored, unforced), naming entries exactly as dict.to-block does (shared helper in dict.rs: symbol key = its name, string key = its text, number key = its rendered text); for any other value returns unit. The render wrapper's native fallback forces RENDER_VIEW(x): a list re-enters the existing block-render code (factored into one helper used by the Block arm too, so a dict carries render tags/metadata like a block); unit goes to EmitNative(x) as before. EMIT natives' Dict arms stay as a defensive error. List keys and stringify-collisions are errors (OPEN 5): DictNotRenderable is replaced by DictKeyNotRenderable (list key, naming it) and DictRenderKeyCollision (keys, rendered name), with hints; error-corpus fixtures for both. Measure the extra intrinsic call on render-heavy benches. TYPING (note §9): lowercase 'dict' type keyword; 'dict(k, v)' = App(App(Con("dict"), k), v), kind * -> * -> *, bare 'dict' = dict(any, any); Display re-sugars; covariant in both (subtype + consistency two-arg arms). Prelude signatures per §9 with tuples for min/max/pop-*; Dict(T) block type untouched (OPEN 9 rename is its own PR, a follow-up). DOCS: prelude reference regenerated; type-checking guide gains dict(k, v); new guide page docs/guide/dicts.md (building, lookup, ordered ops, counting, rendering, priority queue + 141x141 Dijkstra text mirroring bench 023), linked from SUMMARY; export-formats notes dict rendering. The AoC cookbook page (eu-oaz72.16) does not exist yet, so the Dijkstra text lives in the dict guide for the cookbook to link.

2026-11-14 #1198 round 1: both rig-reviews sent back. (1) DictKeyNotRenderable/DictRenderKeyCollision take machine.annotation(), which at render is whatever was last evaluated (e.g. a helper building keys), so the label is wrong; an invalid Smid falls back to the same place, so a correct label likely needs the dict to carry its construction Smid (node/Native layout change) or the render path to track the entry being rendered. (2) Signatures beyond §9's named ones (update/update-strict (v → v), range k → k, get-or default typed v, assoc onto dict.empty/from-block) warn on valid code that passed --strict before; 250_dict.eu goes 0 -> 11 warnings. Reviewer 2: those are choices the plan leaves open -> owner decision (loosen, e.g. get-or k → d → dict(k, v) → v | d, update to (v → any), or accept the warnings). (3) Reviewer 1: RENDER_VIEW returning pairs/unit instead of Block/x (§14) is a deviation from §8 needing owner acceptance; reviewer 2 judged it internal. Non-blocking: symbol-pool growth from rendered keys, lib/reflect.eu has no dict(k, v) case, 'computed once' check in 250_dict untested, DictNotRenderable doc comment.
